text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- The main labour and employers' federations are expected to say today in a joint declaration that joining Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) will require no wage cuts nor dismantling of widely binding collective wage agreements.
- NATO Partnership-for-Peace exercise for 200 to 300 officers from NATO and partnership countries will be held at Tuusula, north of Helsinki, next year. @

- Swedish professor Lars Calmfors, whose government- appointed panel recommended Sweden stay out of EMU at the 1999 start-up, disagrees with Finnish government plan to join single currency early: says high unemployment and one-sided production structure would be risks for Finland in EMU.
- Internal investigation conducted at Russian embassy following last week's reports Russian diplomats smuggled guns out of Finland to Russia.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Banks starting to watch each other for leaks on Bank of Finland's open market activities. @
- Britain's Security Investment Board yesterday gave green light to Swedish pulp derivatives exchange Pulpex, that will be a competitor of Finnish pulp derivatives bourse SOPI.
- Valmet's car-making Valmet Automotive unit is seeking tax and customs relief for its planned car factory to be built in Russia, near the Finnish boarder.
- Finnish power producer IVO's chief executive Heikki Marttinen says IVO and Swedish Vattenfall have not carved the Nordic region into spheres of influence. @
AAMULEHTI
- Finance ministry cut salaries of supreme court judges by 0.7 percent -- Finnish bar association disputes the move.
- New chairman of the Union of Technical Employees in Finland Ilkka Joenpalo calls for wage flexibility, suggests setting wage hike limits for individual sectors.
TURUN SANOMAT
- City of Turku looks likely to sell local telephone company Turun Puhelin to Finnet alliance of regional telephone companies. @
- Unseasonally cold weather has meant a late start for crops in southwestern Finland.
- Finnish defence industry will wither without more orders, review committee says.
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says government will not force municipalities to unite, but that consolidation would bring millions of markka in savings.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 235
